name: American Airlines
planner_tips: Open the search results directly with the deep link https://www.aa.com/booking/search/find-flights?locale=en_US&fareType=Lowest&pax=1&adult=1&type=OneWay&searchType=Revenue&cabin=&carriers=ALL&travelType=personal&slices=<URL-encoded JSON> where slices is like [{"orig":"DFW","origNearby":false,"dest":"AUS","destNearby":false,"date":"2026-05-06"}], since the homepage search form often fails to submit origin and destination. Guest checkout works without logging in; choose Continue as guest on the trip summary page. Payment entry happens at the checkout page under the cart URL, and the trip ends at the credit card form without submitting.
screen_tips: On results, click the cabin card to expand the fare tray, then choose the fare button inside it; choosing Basic Economy opens an upsell where the decline button is labeled Accept restrictions. On the passenger page, add a passenger through the Enter new passenger button and its modal Save button before pressing the page Continue, since Continue earlier just opens the modal; set the state dropdown after country, and use single-letter gender values. On the seat map, the Skip seats for all flights link moves on, and the checkout page has plain fields where card number reveals the CVV field and payment method radios expand the card form.

name: AgentList
planner_tips: Open agentlist.com/?q=TERM to search the directory, or agentlist.com/?q=TERM with the category buttons Skills, Agents, MCPs, Configs or Paid For to narrow results. Sort controls are Top, New and Trending. Individual listings live at agentlist.com/listing/{uuid}. Voting, passkey sign-in and submitting listings need the user's own identity, so only do them when the user explicitly asks for that exact action.
screen_tips: The homepage has a search box at the top and a table with columns #, Title, Author, Date and Votes, with category and sort buttons above it. Typing into the search box can double characters if filled too fast, so after typing confirm the query shows once in the box and the URL becomes agentlist.com/?q=TERM. Listing titles are links to the detail page, and detail pages show the content and a Load box with the skill folder URL. A user pill or Sign out button at the top right means a session is already signed in.

name: Airbnb
planner_tips: Open a search directly with URL parameters: airbnb.com/s/<City>/homes with checkin and checkout dates, adults, min_bedrooms, room_types[]=Entire home/apt, and optional price_max. For stays of 28+ nights, set price_filter_num_nights to the night count; prices then show as monthly totals including fees. Listing pages are airbnb.com/rooms/<id> with check_in, check_out and adults parameters. No login is needed to search or view listings.
screen_tips: Result cards link to /rooms/ pages and show badges such as Guest favorite, Superhost and New place to stay; monthly prices appear as 'monthly' figures on long stays. Cards starting with a date range such as 'Oct 17 to Dec 16' are flexible-date suggestions, not available for the requested dates. Go to the next page with the page-number or cursor controls rather than relying on the Next button, which can fail. The results header shows 'N homes within map area' to confirm the search area.

name: Alaska Airlines
planner_tips: Open https://www.alaskaair.com/search/results?O=SEA&D=PDX&OD=2026-04-29&A=1&C=0&L=0&RT=false to go straight to one-way cash results, bypassing the homepage promo. No login is needed for guest checkout; the flow runs through cart, then Continue as guest at /book/guest-info, then seat selection, then /book/checkout. Results may open in points mode, so switch to Money before choosing a fare.
screen_tips: The Money/Points toggle is a single switch near the top of results. Form fields are custom Auro components: type into text fields after clicking them, and open select dropdowns and click the option rather than relying on typed values. Card number and security code are in separate payment iframes, so click into each field before typing. The Protect your trip insurance section must be set to No before the page will advance.

name: Amazon
planner_tips: Order history is at https://www.amazon.co.uk/your-orders/orders (or amazon.com) and can be filtered with a timeFilter query parameter such as year-2025, months-3 or last30, plus startIndex in steps of 10 for pagination. Order history requires being logged in; if the page redirects to an Amazon Sign-In page, a human must log in first. Product search works directly with https://www.amazon.com/s?k=search+terms and product pages open at /dp/ASIN.
screen_tips: Order history shows 10 orders per page with a total count such as '186 orders' near the top; compare the number of orders you see against that count. A year with no orders may still have a count to check, so verify before concluding it is empty. Use the next-page control at the bottom to move through pages; it is greyed out on the last page. Search results often start with a few sponsored listings, and the first visit to Amazon in a session can need a new tab rather than navigating the current one; pages may take a couple of seconds to finish loading after they appear.

name: Apollo
planner_tips: Company search is at app.apollo.io/#/companies and people search at app.apollo.io/#/people; lists are at app.apollo.io/#/lists and a single list at app.apollo.io/#/lists/<list-id>. Filters are carried in the hash query (for example organizationNumEmployeesRanges[] and organizationIndustryTagIds[]), but only use industry or list IDs seen in the current UI or an observed search URL, never invented ones. Saved searches and lists require a logged-in Apollo account.
screen_tips: The main Save search button overwrites whichever saved search is selected; to make a new one, open Select view and choose Create saved search, and to rename one, hover it in the view selector, open the ellipsis and choose Edit, then select the whole name before typing. When selecting rows, choosing Select this page moves the Apply button up, so find it again afterward, and verify the selected row names before saving. After saving to a list, the page can show duplicate rows or zero counts, so check the individual list and reload the page if counts look wrong; an unfiltered check may need Clear filters because the list page can inherit employee-size filters that hide members.

name: Internet Archive / Wayback Machine
planner_tips: Open web.archive.org/web/*/example.com (with an asterisk) to see the calendar view of captures for a URL, and pick a date from it. Use web.archive.org/web/{YYYYMMDDHHMMSS}/{url} to open a specific snapshot, where a partial timestamp like 20230601 also works. Item pages are archive.org/details/{identifier}, and search is archive.org/advancedsearch.php or the search box on archive.org. No login is needed for public content.
screen_tips: Archived pages show a Wayback toolbar at the top with capture dates and a calendar; click a year or date on the timeline to jump to another capture. Item pages have a download options panel on the right listing files like ZIP, PDF, or MP4. If a snapshot shows a 'Wayback Machine has not archived that URL' message, try a nearby date from the calendar. Search results load on the page, so wait for the result count to appear before reading.

name: Articulate Rise 360
planner_tips: Open authoring at rise.{instance}.articulate.com/authoring/{courseId}/lesson/{lessonId} for any edit, and use the preview URL rise.{instance}.articulate.com/preview/{courseId}#/lessons/{lessonId} only to look at the learner view. Sign-in to the Rise account is required for authoring.
screen_tips: Edits to a lesson save automatically when the side panel is closed, so there is no Save button to look for. Use the X in the panel's top corner to close it, since Escape does not close it. After an edit, reload the page before checking the result, because the preview does not refresh on its own. Code blocks display inside a nested embedded frame, so fonts and styles inside them may look wrong even when the page is correct.

name: ArXiv
planner_tips: Search papers directly at https://arxiv.org/search/?query=transformer&searchtype=all, or use field-specific search like https://arxiv.org/search/?searchtype=title&query=transformer and https://arxiv.org/search/?searchtype=author&query=Vaswani. Open a known paper by ID at https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762 and browse categories at https://arxiv.org/list/cs.LG/recent. No login is needed to read or search papers.
screen_tips: The abstract page shows the title, authors, abstract, and links to the PDF on the left and right sidebars. Search results list papers with their IDs, and each result has a PDF link. Search pages can be sorted and filtered using dropdowns and checkboxes near the top of the results. Reading and searching do not require an account.

name: arXiv
planner_tips: Papers open directly at arxiv.org/abs/<id>, for example arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762, and PDFs at arxiv.org/pdf/<id>. Keyword search works at arxiv.org/search/?query=<terms>&searchtype=all, and category listings at arxiv.org/list/cs.LG/recent. No login is needed to browse, search, or download.
screen_tips: The abstract page shows the title, authors, abstract, and a Download PDF link in the left sidebar. Version history appears under Submission history near the bottom of the abstract page. Search results show 50 per page by default, with pagination controls at the top and bottom. Search fields are on the top bar and the results page has its own search box.

name: Atlas
planner_tips: Log in first, since unauthenticated visits redirect to /sign-in and login uses Google SSO with a passkey and no visible password option. After login the app lands on /home. Open business development pages directly at /business-development/opportunities, /business-development/leads, /business-development/prospects, or /business-development/playbook, and candidates at /candidates. A specific job or project is at /projects/<id>. Opportunity filters can be set through a filters query parameter, but setting them in the UI is simpler.
screen_tips: On /business-development/opportunities, the stage tabs are Identified, Initial Outreach, Late Stage, Converted, and Archived, and the page can switch between kanban and list views. Filter controls are for owner, stage, industry, segment, and conversion probability. Page titles begin with a green dot emoji, such as "🟢 Business development", which can confirm the right page has loaded. If the page bounces to sign-in, the session has expired and you need to log in again in the same browser profile.

name: Big Bang
planner_tips: Open https://www.bigbang.hr/webshop/kosarica/ for the cart and https://www.bigbang.hr/webshop/kupac/ for checkout, which has three steps on the same URL: customer data, delivery method, then payment. Product pages follow https://www.bigbang.hr/webshop/<slug>/<sku>. No login is mentioned in the guide, so guest checkout appears possible.
screen_tips: Customer data fields are First name, Last name, Address, Location, Email and Phone. The Location field is an autocomplete: type a postal code or city and pick the matching suggestion from the dropdown, which then fills in zip code and city. Continue buttons read 'Nastavi na odabir načina dostave', then 'Nastavi na plaćanje', and the final button is 'Potvrdi i naruči'. On the payment step, bank transfer is preselected, so choose card or KEKS Pay explicitly if wanted.

name: Bilbasen
planner_tips: Open search pages directly with the make and model in the path, for example https://www.bilbasen.dk/brugt/bil/vw/id.4?pricefrom=150000&priceto=195000, where pricefrom and priceto are whole DKK amounts. Make and model slugs are lowercase, and the site may redirect to an internal model id, which is fine. Results show about 30 listings per page with a total count, so plan to page through with the next-page control until all results are seen. No login is needed to browse listings.
screen_tips: Search results show listing cards with price, mileage, first registration and fuel type. Use the visible next-page control at the bottom of the results to go further, and wait for the listing set to change before reading the next page. Prices are in DKK and mileage uses a Danish thousands separator, so 76.500 km means 76,500 km. Equipment lists are not on the results page, so open a listing's detail page for features and verify battery or charging claims in the description against the exact variant and model year.

name: Bilibili
planner_tips: Search directly at https://search.bilibili.com/all?keyword={QUERY}, with result tabs like /video or /bangumi reached from the tab bar. Video pages are https://www.bilibili.com/video/{BV_ID}, and personal space is https://space.bilibili.com/{UID} with subpages like /dynamic, /upload, /favlist. Following feed is https://t.bilibili.com/, watch history is https://www.bilibili.com/account/history, and watch later is https://www.bilibili.com/watchlater/#/list; these and favorites, dynamics and messages need a logged-in account, while public pages work without login.
screen_tips: Top nav holds 首页, 番剧, 直播, 游戏中心, 会员购, 漫画, 赛事, and the avatar menu at top right opens 动态, 收藏, 历史, 创作中心. On a video page, the toolbar under the player has 赞 (like), 投币 (coin), 收藏 (favorite) and 分享; allow a few seconds after load before those controls respond. Do not confuse 动态 (following feed at t.bilibili.com) with a user's own 动态 tab in their space. Coins (硬币) are free daily rewards, separate from paid B币.

name: Booking.com
planner_tips: Search results open directly at https://www.booking.com/searchresults.html with query parameters ss (destination text), checkin and checkout as YYYY-MM-DD, group_adults, no_rooms, and selected_currency such as USD, for example ss=Paris&checkin=2026-05-01&checkout=2026-05-03&group_adults=2&no_rooms=1&selected_currency=USD. Sort with order=price or order=review_score and filter with nflt values such as fc=2 for free cancellation or class=4;class=5 for star rating. Hotel pages follow https://www.booking.com/hotel/{country_code}/{hotel-slug}.html and city pages follow https://www.booking.com/city/{country_code}/{city-slug}.html. Browsing is usually not blocked for a normal browser session, but the site may show a cookie consent banner for EU visitors.
screen_tips: Accept the cookie consent banner first if it appears, using the Accept button, before interacting with the page. Results and prices load a few seconds after the page appears, so wait briefly before reading cards. Next-page navigation is on the results page and each page holds 25 results. Prices shown are per night unless the page says otherwise, and taxes may be listed separately near the price.

name: BOSS直聘
planner_tips: Job search is at https://www.zhipin.com/web/geek/jobs and works without login, and city pages use pinyin slugs such as https://www.zhipin.com/shanghai/. Job detail pages are at https://www.zhipin.com/job_detail/{JOB_ID}.html and company pages at https://www.zhipin.com/gongsi/{COMPANY_ID}~.html. Chat is at https://www.zhipin.com/web/geek/chat and requires login. Search filters on the job list are not reflected in the URL, so set them on the page.
screen_tips: In the chat page's left panel, the filter tabs are 全部, 未读(N) and 新招呼, with a 更多 dropdown offering 仅沟通, 有交换, 有面试 and 不感兴趣. Click a conversation in the left list to open its message history on the right, and wait about 2 seconds for it to render. Never send a message unless the user explicitly asks you to. On job cards, salary digits render as unreadable symbols in the DOM, so read the salary visually from the screen.

name: Browser Use Cloud
planner_tips: The dashboard root cloud.browser-use.com redirects to /signup when logged out, so log in first; /dashboard, /browsers, /profiles and /api-keys are unverified guesses, so check the sidebar after login rather than trusting those paths. Live browser sessions show a liveUrl on live.browser-use.com, which is a separate host from the dashboard. Billing and organisation/team admin are not covered by this site guide, and aggregate usage is not shown as a simple page.
screen_tips: After login, navigate using the sidebar links rather than typed paths, since slugs other than /signup were not verified. Session and profile pages are per-item views reached from their lists. Cost figures appear as dollar amounts on each browser record, and a stopped session shows a finished time with no live link.

name: Capterra
planner_tips: Product pages use the form capterra.com/p/{id}/{Slug}/ with reviews at /p/{id}/{Slug}/reviews/, pricing at /pricing/, and alternatives at /alternatives/; Slug is case-sensitive, so find the exact ID and slug from a category listing rather than guessing. Category pages are at capterra.com/{category}-software/, for example capterra.com/project-management-software/, with ?page=N for more results, and the full category list is at capterra.com/categories/. Site search via /search/?q= does not work, so browse categories or open product URLs directly. Reading public pages needs no login; only the review-writing flow and account areas require signing in.
screen_tips: Use the category and product pages to find products, then open the Reviews tab for ratings and written reviews. Reviews show 25 per page, with page navigation at the bottom of the list. Ratings, review counts, and sentiment appear near the top of the product page. Some pages may show a Cloudflare verification challenge; wait for it to clear before reading the content.

name: CentileBrain
planner_tips: Open https://centilebrain.org/#/model to reach the tool; no login or account is needed. Choose a modality (Subcortical Volume, Cortical Thickness, or Surface Area) and a sex, then upload a single .xlsx file that follows the site's template for that modality and sex, which you must download from the site first. Compute can take 30 to 90 seconds, and results come back as a zip download containing per-subject z-score CSVs. Batch uploads of many subjects work in one run.
screen_tips: The modality buttons and sex toggles sit at the top of the page and change the embedded app below them; after switching, wait a few seconds for the new app to load before interacting. The upload control, an email field (any valid-looking address works), and a Compute button are inside that embedded app, which may scroll out of view, so scroll to find them. Compute is done when the page shows 'Computation complete', and then a Download Results link appears to save the zip.

name: Claude
planner_tips: Organization custom connectors are managed at claude.ai/admin-settings/connectors, which requires an Owner account on a Team or Enterprise plan; check the organization selector first. Personal claude.ai/settings/connectors may redirect to a modal saying connectors moved to Customize, which is not the admin page. Skills are at claude.ai/customize/skills, and an existing skill's page is claude.ai/customize/skills/<skill_id>, so find the ID from the current page; the contents view is that path with /contents appended.
screen_tips: To add a custom connector, open Add, hover the Custom row, and choose Web; the dialog takes a name and MCP URL first, then a second step for auth, where OAuth with a pre-registered client uses Sign in now and Use your own OAuth client. An unauthenticated 401 from the MCP server is normal for OAuth. To update a skill, use the overflow menu's Replace option rather than Add, which creates a duplicate; after saving, reload and reopen Contents, check the version selector marks the new version current, and note the page may show an older version. Uploaded skills appear in Chat and Cowork mode, not necessarily in Code mode.

name: Claude
planner_tips: Shared conversation links look like claude.ai/share/<uuid>. The share page only shows the chat text when the browser is signed into claude.ai, so use a Chrome profile that is already logged in. Live chats at claude.ai/chat/<uuid> are a different page and are not covered by these tips.
screen_tips: If the share page loads but the conversation body is blank, the session is logged out, so sign in first. The conversation title is in the page header area at the top, not in the browser tab title, which just says Claude. Messages alternate as separate blocks with no wrapper per turn, and user messages may show a duplicated preview heading above the text. Attachments and artifacts in a shared chat are not shown in full on the page.

name: CoinGecko
planner_tips: Human-facing pages live on coingecko.com; coin pages follow coingecko.com/en/coins/{coin-slug} (for example coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin), and the homepage lists top coins by market cap. Search is available from the top bar at coingecko.com and results show a coin's rank and price. No login is needed to view prices, charts, or coin details.
screen_tips: The main coin list is a table sorted by market cap rank, with price, 1h, 24h, 7d, market cap and volume columns; click a column header to sort. On a coin page, the price and 24h change sit at the top, with the chart below and currency or timeframe toggles above it. Search results open a dropdown under the search box, so click the matching coin name rather than pressing Enter. Dismiss any cookie or promotional banner before reading the numbers.

name: CoinMarketCap
planner_tips: Coin pages open at coinmarketcap.com/currencies/{slug}/ (for example /currencies/bitcoin/), and the homepage at coinmarketcap.com/ lists the top 100 coins. Public market data needs no login. The pro-api subdomain requires a paid key, so avoid it.
screen_tips: On a coin page, price and stats such as market cap, volume and supply appear near the top, and the 24h and 7d percent changes sit beside the price. Search is at the top of the page and lists matching coins as you type. Numbers are in USD unless a currency selector shows otherwise.

name: Coursera
planner_tips: Open https://www.coursera.org/search?query=KEYWORD to search courses by keyword; the results load client-side, so wait a few seconds before reading them. Individual courses are at https://www.coursera.org/learn/COURSE-SLUG. Course pages show content without login, while enrolling and certificates require a Coursera account login.
screen_tips: Search results appear as course cards after a short async load, so wait before judging the page is empty. The search box is at the top of the page and accepts typed queries with Enter. A course page's title and details are visible on screen without signing in; enroll buttons may prompt for login.

name: Craigslist
planner_tips: Open search pages directly at https://{city}.craigslist.org/search/{category}?query=KEYWORDS, using city subdomains such as sfbay, newyork, chicago, losangeles, seattle, boston, miami, denver, austin, portland, sandiego, or phoenix. Category codes include sss (for sale), ela (electronics), fua (furniture), cto (cars by owner), apa (apartments), roo (rooms), jjj (jobs), bbb (services), and eve (events). Add filters as query parameters: min_price, max_price, sort=date, sort=priceasc, sort=pricedsc, and condition=10 through 60. Browsing and searching need no login, but posting or messaging does.
screen_tips: Search results list listings with title, price, and neighborhood; click a title to open the full post with price, description, and photos. Results may show a bit more than the filters imply, so check the price on each post. Pagination appears as next and previous arrows at the top or bottom of results, and the page count updates when you move. Contact buttons reveal a reply option that may require a login or a CAPTCHA, so expect a verification step before the reply shows.

name: CrossRef
planner_tips: CrossRef is a metadata database with no login; the browser is not needed for it, but a DOI can be opened directly at https://doi.org/DOI (for example https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-021-03819-2) to reach the publisher page. Search works at https://api.crossref.org/works?query=KEYWORDS, and the public search UI is not a page to use for bulk results. Journal lookups by ISSN are at https://api.crossref.org/journals/ISSN.
screen_tips: The site has no real interactive UI for this data; the API returns raw JSON in the browser, so read the text on screen rather than looking for buttons. Titles are lists, so the first entry is the main title. If a DOI is invalid the page shows a 404 error rather than a result.

name: Ctrip
planner_tips: Open https://hotels.ctrip.com/hotels/list?flexType=1&cityId=2&provinceId=0&districtId=0&countryId=1&checkin=YYYY-MM-DD&checkout=YYYY-MM-DD for domestic hotel prices (cityId 2 is Shanghai, 1 Beijing, 32 Guangzhou, 30 Shenzhen); prices show without login when the full parameter set is present. Do not use a shortened URL with city= instead of cityId=, since that redirects to passport.ctrip.com login. If unsure of a cityId, start at https://hotels.ctrip.com/ and search the city there, then read the resulting list URL. Hotel detail pages open at https://hotels.ctrip.com/hotel/<hotelId>.html?checkin=...&checkout=... without login.
screen_tips: The list is a set of hotel cards with names, scores, and a price pair like ¥original ¥current followed by 起 meaning from-price; the current price is the lower one. Review counts such as 1,234条点评 are not prices. The homepage defaults to the overseas tab with no prices, so switch to domestic results or use the list URL. The search button on the homepage is a div, so click it by position rather than relying on a button. If the page moves to a login screen, stop and ask the user rather than entering credentials.

name: Stripe Dashboard
planner_tips: The guide only points to a separate page about test mode and sandboxes, so no direct URLs or login details are given here.
screen_tips: The guide gives no on-screen details for this site beyond a pointer to test mode and sandboxes.

name: DEV Community
planner_tips: Public articles open at dev.to/{username}/{slug}, and a user's profile is at dev.to/{username}. Reading articles, tags, profiles and comments needs no login. Listing your own feed with the state=all filter requires logging in.
screen_tips: Articles can have no cover image, so do not expect a header picture on every post. Comments are nested, so replies sit under their parent comment. Reaction and comment counts are on the article list and page. Timestamps like published dates may show only month and day with no year.

name: DoorDash
planner_tips: Search results are relative to the delivery address on the account, so check the ZIP shown before trusting results. Store pages open directly at doordash.com/convenience/store/<store_id>, and a single product opens at doordash.com/convenience/store/<store_id>/product/<item_id>, which redirects to the store with that product's panel open. The cross-store product page is doordash.com/browse/products/<product_id>. Searching is done at doordash.com/search/store/<query>/, which loads results server-side. Browsing needs a logged-in account.
screen_tips: Search results load on the search page and group into sections like Get it now, Top savings, and All results, then one carousel per store; the same item can appear in several sections. Product cards show price, a stock or discount badge, and a rating; clicking a card opens a product modal showing the price at each nearby store and the delivery time. Results are loose matches, so compare product names yourself. If the page shows a login prompt or bot check, stop and report it.}

name: DuckDuckGo
planner_tips: The guide covers only the DuckDuckGo Instant Answer API, a scripted JSON endpoint that is not a search engine, so there are no browser-facing tips for planning page URLs. For ordinary web searches, open duckduckgo.com/?q=your+query in a browser instead.
screen_tips: The source guide advises against using a browser for this API, so no on-screen tips apply. Normal duckduckgo.com search pages need no login.

name: eBay
planner_tips: Search directly with a URL like https://www.ebay.com/sch/i.html?_nkw=QUERY, using plus signs for spaces. Add LH_BIN=1 for Buy It Now only, LH_Auction=1 for auctions, LH_ItemCondition=1000 for new items, and _sop=15 to sort by lowest price plus shipping. Item pages are at https://www.ebay.com/itm/LISTING_ID. Browsing and searching need no login, but buying requires an eBay account sign-in.
screen_tips: Pages are ordinary eBay search and item pages, with results as cards showing title, price, and a strikethrough original price when discounted. Prices appear in the visitor's local currency, so read the currency symbol instead of assuming dollars. If the page says Pardon Our Interruption or shows an Access Denied error, stop, wait a minute or two, and reload rather than retrying quickly. A 'No exact matches found' note means the results are loose substitutes, not what was searched for.

name: Etsy
planner_tips: Open search pages directly with https://www.etsy.com/search?q=keywords&explicit=1, using + for spaces, and add &order=price_asc, &order=newest, or &min_price and &max_price for filtering. Listing pages look like https://www.etsy.com/listing/ID/slug, and shop pages look like https://www.etsy.com/shop/ShopName with exact capitalization. Etsy sometimes shows a bot-check challenge to automated visitors, so expect a real browser session to be needed. Buying, favoriting, or messaging sellers requires logging in.
screen_tips: Search results show listing cards with title, price, and shop name, and clicking a card opens its listing page. Shop listings load more items by scrolling down or pressing a Load more button rather than through a numbered pager. Pages render slowly after load, so wait a few seconds before reading prices or titles. Ads in results are marked with a sponsored label and are not regular matches.

name: Eventbrite
planner_tips: Browse listings directly at https://www.eventbrite.com/d/{state}--{city}/{category}/ such as https://www.eventbrite.com/d/ca--san-francisco/tech/, with optional filters like /free--events/ or /events--this-weekend/ in place of the category. Date range can be added as ?start_date=YYYY-MM-DD&end_date=YYYY-MM-DD, and results continue on ?page=2. Individual event pages use the form https://www.eventbrite.com/e/{slug}-tickets-{id}. Browsing and buying tickets works without login, but purchasing or viewing account details requires signing in.
screen_tips: Event cards on listing pages link to event detail pages, where date, venue, price, and the ticket selection sit near the top. Date filters narrow results but may still show events outside the chosen range, so check each event's date on its page. Free events show a price of zero rather than a blank field. A ticket selection only takes effect after the quantity is changed with its plus or minus control, and the checkout step appears after clicking the ticket button.

name: Expedia
planner_tips: Build searches with URL parameters instead of the UI: hotel search at https://www.expedia.co.in/Hotel-Search?destination={city or hotel}&startDate=YYYY-MM-DD&endDate=YYYY-MM-DD&rooms=1&adults=N&children=N&childrenAges=5,7 and flight search at https://www.expedia.ca/Flights-Search?flight-type=roundtrip&mode=search&trip=roundtrip&leg1=from:YYZ,to:ICN,departure:2027/07/03TANYT&leg2=from:ICN,to:YYZ,departure:2027/07/25TANYT&passengers=adults:1&options=cabin:economy&sort=price%3Aa. Property pages can be opened as https://www.expedia.mx/{slug}.h{hotelId}.Informacion-Hotel with optional startDate, endDate and rm1 query parameters, and the slug is cosmetic. Expedia may block datacenter IPs and can show captchas, so a logged-in or residential browser session is more reliable.
screen_tips: Do not use the date picker; it closes on coordinate clicks, so set dates through the URL instead. The travellers panel and Done button respond better to direct element clicks than to coordinate clicks. Expedia's stop checkboxes are exclusive, so nonstop and 1 stop must be clicked one at a time, waiting several seconds for each reload. Do not click Search on a page that was opened with a prefilled search URL, since that resets filters; the price filter applies after pressing Enter in the max price field.

name: Facebook Groups and Pages
planner_tips: Group feeds open at facebook.com/groups/{slug_or_id}/?sorting_setting=CHRONOLOGICAL so posts are sorted newest first; the joined-groups list is at facebook.com/groups/joins/. Page posts open at facebook.com/{vanity_or_id}/posts, and Page search is facebook.com/search/pages/?q={query}. Viewing a group requires being logged in and a member of that group, and logged-out views show a stripped page with no posts. Pages are public but logged-in is recommended, since logged-out views add login prompts that interrupt scrolling.
screen_tips: Posts are div[role=article] blocks; click a 'See more' control on long posts before reading their text. Feeds unload posts as you scroll, so read them as you scroll rather than after. A login, checkpoint, or device-verification screen means stop and let the user handle it. Using the page as a logged-in member is the normal mode, and there is no post, reply, or message action in this guide to rely on.

name: Feishu Docs
planner_tips: Feishu document URLs look like https://<tenant>.feishu.cn/docx/<token>, and the tenant name is the first hostname label. Sibling documents in the same wiki are linked inside the body text, so open them by clicking those links rather than guessing URLs. Use an already logged-in browser session; no login steps are needed.
screen_tips: The document content scrolls inside an inner div, not the window, so scroll that container and expect content to render slowly, waiting about a second after each scroll. Tables lose their column structure in plain text, so read tables from screenshots. Tables and images only appear reliably when scrolled into view, and some fixed UI text such as Share, Comments, and Help Center is page chrome, not document content.

name: Figma
planner_tips: Figma file comments are shown on the file's design page, reached via a figma.com/design/<FILE_KEY>/<slug> share URL; the file key is the middle segment of that URL. Opening a design URL may bounce to an 'Open in Figma app' interstitial, and the user may need to sign in to Figma to see comments.
screen_tips: If a 'Opened in Figma app' or 'Open here instead' interstitial appears, click 'Open here instead' to continue in the browser. Comments are listed in the comments panel, and a comment's resolved state is shown as a check mark on its thread; replies appear nested under their parent thread.

name: FlightHub
planner_tips: Open the search page directly at https://www.flighthub.com/flight/search with query parameters seg0_from and seg0_to for airport codes, seg1_from and seg1_to for the return leg (reversed), seg0_date and seg1_date as YYYY-MM-DD, type=roundtrip, num_adults, seat_class=Economy, currency (usd or cad), and order_by=cheapest, fastest or best. Example: seg0_from=YYZ&seg0_to=ICN&seg1_from=ICN&seg1_to=YYZ. Searching does not require a login. The site sits behind Cloudflare, so a normal browser session is needed.
screen_tips: The home page search form's date picker does not respond to clicks, so avoid it and use the search URL instead. Airport fields accept typed codes, and a dropdown may appear that needs Tab or Enter before moving on. The search button is a div, not a real button. Results load over 10 to 30 seconds behind a searching dialog; wait for it to close, then read the flight cards showing airline, times, stops, duration, price and a Select button.

name: Flipkart
planner_tips: Search directly via https://www.flipkart.com/search?q=QUERY with spaces as + and optional price filters like &p%5B%5D=facets.price_range.to%3D500 for a maximum price, plus &sort=price_asc to sort by price. Category browsing works at paths like https://www.flipkart.com/toys/pr?sid=tng. Changing the delivery pincode on some product pages requires logging in, so search results show the default delivery estimate instead.
screen_tips: A login/signup popup appears on every new visit and blocks everything until closed; close its X button at the top right of the modal or press Escape. Product pages may show a zoom image overlay that swallows clicks, so press Escape to clear it before retrying. Price and rating filters are in the left sidebar, and clicking them re-renders the list, so check the results update before continuing. Prices use the rupee sign with Indian comma grouping, such as ₹1,23,456.

name: Framer
planner_tips: Project editor URLs look like framer.com/projects/<project-slug>-<id>, and the user must already be logged in with the project open. The Publish button only appears after selecting a page in the Pages tab, so plan to open the Pages tab and pick the page before publishing. Changes to page settings, SEO fields, redirects, font or image uploads, drag-and-drop layout, and smart component variants cannot be done reliably by an agent and should be handed to the user as step-by-step instructions.
screen_tips: Use the left rail tabs (Pages, Layers, Assets) to navigate; the Publish button is in the top-right and is only visible when a page is selected in the Pages tab, not while the code editor is open. Opening a code file requires a double-click on its asset row, and a single click only selects it. Pasting code into the Monaco editor works best by selecting all and pasting, then waiting a few seconds before saving, and check for red error underlines afterwards. Live site changes may take 30 to 60 seconds to appear, so add a query parameter like ?v=timestamp when checking the published page.

name: FRED
planner_tips: Open https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/SERIESID for a single series page, such as /series/GDP or /series/UNRATE, and use https://fred.stlouisfed.org/search?st=QUERY to search series by keyword. Series IDs are exact and case-sensitive, so use uppercase like GDP, CPIAUCSL, FEDFUNDS, DGS10 or SP500. No login is needed to view public series pages, but downloading data or using the API key requires a free registered St. Louis Fed account.
screen_tips: On a series page the chart sits at the top, with date-range buttons such as 1Y, 5Y, 10Y and Max above it and a Download control to export data. Data values appear in the observations table lower on the page, and it can be sorted or switched between frequencies. Typing an ID directly in the search box and pressing Enter opens the matching series page.

name: Frontier Airlines
planner_tips: Start at https://www.flyfrontier.com/ and search with the homepage widget; deep links into booking.flyfrontier.com return 404, so do not guess booking URLs. The booking flow runs in order: Select (fares), Passengers, Bundles, SeatMap, Bags, Extras, then Payment. Stop before final payment submission unless the user authorizes that specific purchase. Membership pricing (Discount Den) is not granted just by declining a membership upsell, so choose the fare matching the user's membership and verify the final total before paying.
screen_tips: On the homepage, pick one-way, type the airport in the origin and destination fields and choose the suggestion from the list, then set the date with the date picker rather than typing it, and click the Search button. On the fare page, click the label around the fare, not just the radio, then press the Continue button for that fare type; if the Discount Den offer appears, close it with its No Thanks button, since the X icon does nothing. Modals on bundles, seats, bags and extras are dismissed by their 'continue without' buttons; the Extras page needs both the free agent-assist option and the decline option in the disruption assistance frame selected before continuing. Payment fields are ordinary inputs, but the expiration year uses two digits and the card number auto-formats dashes.

name: Furnished Finder
planner_tips: City search pages use the form www.furnishedfinder.com/housing/us--<state>--<city-slug>, for example www.furnishedfinder.com/housing/us--ca--san-francisco; the URL /housing/San-Francisco-CA redirects to the homepage, so do not use it. Each listing is at www.furnishedfinder.com/property/<listingId>, where the id looks like 1044041_1. Search results show only the first 72 listings per view, so split a wide area into smaller map boxes and open each one, using a map parameter with min and max latitude and longitude and searchType=REGIONAL. Browsing and property pages are anonymous, but sending a booking inquiry requires an account.
screen_tips: Result cards list the rent, bedrooms, and an Available or Recently added badge; filter to entire units because rooms are mixed into results. Listing locations are fuzzed by up to about 0.5 km, so confirm the neighborhood from the description or the Closest facilities distances on the property page. Titles can overstate bedroom counts, such as '1BR + Office' being listed as two bedrooms, so check the details. The Calendar updated date shows how current the landlord's availability is, and many older dates indicate stale listings. The similar rentals strip at the bottom of a property page can show listings outside the area you searched.

name: G2
planner_tips: Open product reviews directly at www.g2.com/products/{slug}/reviews, using a lowercase hyphenated product slug such as slack or microsoft-teams; add ?page=2 for more reviews. Category listings are at www.g2.com/categories/{slug}, and comparisons at www.g2.com/compare/{slug1}-vs-{slug2}. Reading reviews and product pages needs no login, but scrolling far past the first few reviews triggers a sign-in modal, so use ?page=N instead.
screen_tips: The site is protected by an invisible bot check that resolves on its own; wait about 5 seconds after load and confirm the tab title is not just "g2.com" before reading content. If a sign-in overlay appears after scrolling, close it with its X button and continue using page-number URLs. Review cards show star rating, title, pros and cons text, reviewer job title and date, and the rating breakdown is near the top of the reviews page. Pages can take a few seconds to fill in, so wait and re-check if the content looks empty.

name: Gemini Spark skills
planner_tips: Open gemini.google.com/spark/skills to find and edit skills. Editing requires being logged into Gemini. To recover an earlier skill version, open the completed Spark conversation that created or last edited that skill, since its confirmation cards keep the skill content.
screen_tips: Find the skill card whose title exactly matches the intended name, since a partial match can select a similarly named skill. The editor has Skill description and Skill instructions fields plus Save skill and Skills, go back buttons. After saving, wait for the Skill saved notice to disappear before going back, or a misleading Leave without saving dialog may appear; reopen the skill afterward to verify the saved text.

name: Genius
planner_tips: Song lyrics pages use the form genius.com/{Artist}-{song-slug}-lyrics, and artist pages use genius.com/artists/{Artist}. Search results are rendered client-side, so for a search open genius.com and type the query into the search box rather than relying on a /search?q= URL, which shows unrelated trending songs. No login is needed to read songs, lyrics, or artist pages; login is only needed for personal features like library, editing, or annotation tools.
screen_tips: The search box is at the top of the page; typing a query shows a dropdown of matching songs, artists, and albums to click. Lyrics are shown in blocks with section headers like [Verse 1] and [Chorus], and annotated words are highlighted and clickable to open annotation popups. Song pages list the primary album under the song details, and the album shown there may be a compilation rather than the original release. Pressing Enter in the search box runs the full search and shows result sections for each type.

name: GitHub
planner_tips: Repo pages live at github.com/owner/repo and the trending page at github.com/trending, optionally github.com/trending/python?since=weekly. Starring, watching, and other repo changes require the user to be logged in to GitHub. Read-only repo facts like stars and forks are easiest to read from the public page or the repo's REST API rather than the rendered DOM.
screen_tips: On a repo page the Star and Watch buttons sit in the header at the top right; the page may show a second hidden copy of the Star button in a sticky header, so use the visible one. Clicking the visible Star button in the page may not register, so check the result by reloading and seeing whether the button now reads Unstar or Starred. Trending repos appear as cards with the repo name as a link, a description, language, total stars, and stars gained in the period. The star count inside a button can lag briefly after an action, so wait about a second and scroll to the top before judging whether it worked.

name: Glassdoor
planner_tips: Open company reviews at glassdoor.com/Reviews/{Company-slug}-Reviews-E{employer_id}.htm, for example glassdoor.com/Reviews/Google-Reviews-E9079.htm, and the overview at glassdoor.com/Overview/Working-at-{Company-slug}-EI_IE{employer_id}.htm. Job search works with glassdoor.com/Job/jobs.htm?sc.keyword=software+engineer, adding &locT=C&locKeyword={city} for a city or &remoteWorkType=1 for remote, and &p=2 for later pages. Salary pages use glassdoor.com/Salaries/{role-slug}-salary-SRCH_KO0,{length of role slug}.htm. Many pages show only a limited preview without a sign-in.
screen_tips: A sign-in modal appears on reviews and salary pages as you scroll, so close it with its X button before scrolling further; the X may fall off screen once you scroll. A cookie consent banner may cover the page at first, so accept or dismiss it. The page may briefly show a Cloudflare security check titled Security before the real content loads; wait a few seconds and reload if it persists. Job cards are listed on the left with details on the right, and clicking a card updates the right panel.

name: Gmail
planner_tips: Open https://mail.google.com and make sure the account is already logged in. Compose uses the left-rail Compose button or the 'c' shortcut, so planners should not expect a direct compose URL to be reliable.
screen_tips: Pressing 'c' opens a compose window with the To field focused. Do not press Tab between fields, since Tab inserts a tab character into To; click the Subject and body fields instead. Minimized drafts appear as small bars at the bottom of the page, so act only on the large open compose window. Recipients become chips once focus leaves the To field, and the Send button is in the compose window's bottom bar; a 'Message sent' toast confirms sending.}

name: Goodreads
planner_tips: Search books at goodreads.com/search?q=QUERY&search_type=books, and book pages open at goodreads.com/book/show/BOOK_ID with the numeric ID from the URL. Author pages are at goodreads.com/author/show/AUTHOR_ID and list lists at goodreads.com/list/show/LIST_ID; the browsing needs no login.
screen_tips: Search results show each book's title, author, average rating and rating count, and clicking a title opens its book page. Book pages show ratings, genres, description and series near the top, and the description may need a 'more' click to expand. Confirm you are on the intended book by checking the title and author before acting.

name: Google Flights
planner_tips: Open https://www.google.com/travel/flights?tfs=<encoded>&hl=en&curr=USD where tfs encodes the search; the tfs value is a base64 blob, so for one-way or round trip trips, a simpler route is typing airports and dates into the form at google.com/travel/flights. Multi-city searches need trip type set to multi-city with one leg per segment. No login is needed to search or view prices.
screen_tips: The first results page shows only leg 1 and each price is labelled entire trip, which is an estimate that can be lower than any bookable total, so click a leg 1 row and read the leg 2 page for the real number. After clicking through, wait several seconds for the list to load before concluding there are no flights. Use the Sorted by control and choose Price, then confirm the sort label changed. Check cabin suffixes like Economy + Premium Economy on each row before quoting a fare, and confirm the passenger count and total on the final page.

name: Google Sheets
planner_tips: Open spreadsheets at docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<id>/edit and log in with the Google account first, since editing and CSV export need an authorized session. To verify written values, open docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<id>/export?format=csv&gid=<gid> and check the contents; an account chooser or login page means the session is not authorized.
screen_tips: Autocomplete can silently change a typed text value: a suggested remainder from the same column is selected, and Tab or Enter commits it, so press Delete after typing a text value and before Tab or Enter. Do not press Delete after the cell is committed, since it may clear the selected cell. Navigate to a cell by typing its address (for example A2) in the Name Box at the top left and pressing Enter rather than clicking grid coordinates. Verify each entered value by reading the cell back, including numbers, dates, and URLs, because a wrong autocomplete value looks like a successful entry.

name: Project Gutenberg
planner_tips: Search the catalog at gutenberg.org/ebooks/search/?query=TERMS&sort_order=downloads, or use query prefixes like author:dickens or title:... in the same query box. Open a book directly at gutenberg.org/ebooks/ID using its numeric ID, and read the plain text at gutenberg.org/ebooks/ID.txt.utf-8. Browse a genre shelf at gutenberg.org/ebooks/bookshelf/ID. No login is needed for reading or downloading.
screen_tips: Search results show book titles and authors as links; click the title to open the book page with its download formats listed. The plain-text link is labeled Plain Text UTF-8 and opens the full book text in the browser. Results show 25 per page, with a next link at the bottom to continue.

name: Hacker News
planner_tips: Open https://news.ycombinator.com for the front page and https://news.ycombinator.com/?p=2 for later pages; no login is needed for page 2, but page 3 and beyond require a login. For keyword searches, use https://hn.algolia.com/?q=KEYWORD (add &type=story or &sort=byDate for story results sorted by date). Item threads open at https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=ID.
screen_tips: The front page lists stories in rank order, each with a title link, a points count, and a comments link at the bottom of its row; job posts have no points or author. Click the comments link to open a thread, where all comments load on one page with no pagination. Titles can look odd in raw text because of HTML entities, but they display correctly on screen. Hacker News has no JavaScript-dependent loading, so a page is ready as soon as it appears and clicks give instant results.

name: HowLongToBeat
planner_tips: Game pages open at howlongtobeat.com/game/{game_id} using a numeric ID, not a slug, so search first to find the ID. Site search is at howlongtobeat.com with the query typed into the search box on the home page. No login is needed to view completion times.
screen_tips: Completion times are shown as Main Story, Main + Extras, and Completionist, in hours. A time of blank or zero means no submissions exist for that category. Search results mix base games with DLC and expansions, so check the type label before picking a result. The top result is usually the intended game when results are sorted by popularity.

name: HubSpot
planner_tips: Open https://app-<region>.hubspot.com/private-apps/{portalId}/{appId}/edit to edit a Private App's webhook subscriptions, where region is na1, na2, eu1 and so on; the read-only https://app-<region>.hubspot.com/private-apps/{portalId}/{appId}/webhooks page cannot create subscriptions. Use the edit page's Webhooks tab to add or remove property-change subscriptions, then open the read-only /webhooks URL to verify. The user must be logged into their HubSpot account with access to the portal.
screen_tips: In edit mode, click the Webhooks tab in the left sidebar, then Create subscription to open the right drawer. Object type and event type are dropdowns that often need a real mouse click on the option, not a script click; choose the object, choose Property changed, pick the property, then click Subscribe in the drawer. Subscribe only adds a draft row, so click Commit changes at the top right to save; the page then leaves edit mode, and the new row should appear on the read-only Webhooks page. Changes can take a few seconds or up to five minutes to take effect.

name: iHerb
planner_tips: Product pages use the form iherb.com/pr/<descriptive-slug>/<numeric-item-id>; the numeric ID identifies the exact item, so verify it and the selected package rather than substituting a similar name. Plain fetch often works, and labels need no login, but cart or account actions require signing in.
screen_tips: The product heading is the selected product name, and the package or count selector sits near the buying panel. Supplement Facts may be already visible in a table or hidden behind a collapsed header; scroll to the header, click it, and confirm the table is visible before reading it. A 'Similar Recommendation' price belongs to another product, and subscription, one-time and promo prices appear together, so check the purchase type before reading a price.

name: IMDb
planner_tips: Open https://www.imdb.com/chart/top/ for the Top 250 ranked films and https://www.imdb.com/chart/moviemeter/ for the 100 trending titles. Search titles with https://www.imdb.com/find/?s=tt&q=KEYWORD (s=tt limits results to titles). Title pages live at https://www.imdb.com/title/tt{id}/ and the 'More Like This' recommendations there only appear after scrolling down. No login is needed for charts, search, or title pages.
screen_tips: On chart and search pages each row is a list item with the rank prefixed to the title, such as '1. The Shawshank Redemption'. The 'More Like This' section sits far down a title page and loads only after scrolling, so scroll down and wait before looking for it. Vote counts appear abbreviated in parentheses, like (3.1M). Search results can mix people and companies unless the s=tt filter is in the URL.

name: itch.io
planner_tips: Browse URLs open directly: itch.io/games/top-rated, /newest, /featured, /on-sale, /free, and tag listings at itch.io/games/tag-puzzle (use tag-<slug>). Pagination uses ?page=N. Search is at itch.io/search?q=platformer. Combined sort plus tag paths like /games/top-rated/tag-puzzle do not work, so open the tag page and sort from there. Owner dashboards and the API require a login or API key, while browsing and game pages are public.
screen_tips: Game pages show a info table with status, platforms, genre, tags and links, and a price tag only for paid games. Search results beyond page 1 load through a load-more or scroll action rather than page links. Rating and download counts may be missing on tag listing cards, so open the game page to check ratings. Some titles start with an invisible zero-width space that can look like a blank character.

name: JetBlue
planner_tips: Open flight search directly at https://www.jetblue.com/booking/flights with from, to (IATA codes), depart (YYYY-MM-DD), adults=1, children=0, infants=0, roundTripFaresFlag=false and usePoints=false query parameters instead of using the home page form. Guest checkout works without signing in, so no login is needed; cart is at https://www.jetblue.com/booking/cart and checkout at https://www.jetblue.com/booking/checkout. Stop before final payment submission unless the user explicitly authorizes that purchase.
screen_tips: On search results, click a flight card to expand fares, then choose a Select button; a modal then offers Select Blue Basic or Select Blue, and Blue Basic goes straight to the cart. On traveler details, use Continue as guest, fill the form, and use the Title, Gender and date-of-birth dropdowns; the Year list is long, so scroll the target option into view before clicking. On Seats & Extras, Skip to Review & Pay skips seat selection, and card number and CVV are in separate cross-origin TokenEx iframes that often ignore typed input, so wait a few seconds after the page loads and verify the fields are filled before continuing.

name: Indeed, Glassdoor, Stepstone
planner_tips: Open job searches directly by URL instead of typing in the homepage search box: Indeed uses https://www.indeed.com/jobs?q=KEYWORD&l=LOCATION, with fromage=1, 3 or 7 for recent postings, jt=fulltime or jt=parttime for job type, and start=10 for the next page. Glassdoor uses https://www.glassdoor.com/Job/jobs.htm?sc.keyword=KEYWORD, with p=2 for the next page. Stepstone (Germany) uses https://www.stepstone.de/jobs/KEYWORD-WORDS-JOINED-BY-DASHES/in-CITY.html with /page-2.html for later pages. Public browsing needs no login for any of these, though Glassdoor may show a sign-in prompt after a few listings.
screen_tips: Indeed and Glassdoor may show a cookie consent overlay on first load; close it with the Accept button before reading results. Glassdoor often shows a sign-in modal after a few scrolls, so read the visible listings first and close the modal with its X if it blocks the page. Indeed may show a CAPTCHA page that looks like a normal page with a puzzle or a continue button; if results look empty, check for that. Stepstone shows a fullscreen consent layer that must be accepted (look for Alle akzeptieren) before anything else is clickable.

name: Letterboxd
planner_tips: Open film pages directly at letterboxd.com/film/{slug}/ using a lowercase title with hyphens for spaces, and append -{year} when the title is ambiguous (e.g. parasite-2019). Ratings histogram at letterboxd.com/film/{slug}/ratings/, reviews at /film/{slug}/reviews/, popular films at letterboxd.com/films/popular/, and user watched films at letterboxd.com/{username}/films/ are browser-only pages. Browsing pages and user sub-pages may require a login or fail for anonymous visitors, so check the page loads before relying on it. There is no public search URL, so construct the film slug from the title.
screen_tips: Film pages show the title, year, director, rating and synopsis without login. Lists and filter pages load film posters that appear after the page renders, so wait a couple of seconds before reading them. Sub-pages like reviews and ratings can be blocked or show a login prompt for anonymous visitors. Login uses a form protected by Cloudflare Turnstile, which can need a manual check before submitting.

name: LinkedIn
planner_tips: Open https://www.linkedin.com/mynetwork/invitation-manager/received/ for all pending invitations, or append PEOPLE_WITH_MUTUAL_CONNECTION or PEOPLE_WITH_MUTUAL_SCHOOL to the path to filter them. The page requires a logged-in LinkedIn account.
screen_tips: Each invitation card has an Accept and an Ignore button; the filter chip at the top shows the remaining count in parentheses. Some cards labeled 'follows you and is inviting you to connect' have an Accept link that may not work, so use Ignore for those. After accepting a batch, reload the page because the next invitations do not load automatically. A 'Take care when connecting' dialog may appear; click 'Accept invite' to continue.

name: Loom
planner_tips: Private workspace library folders are at loom.com/looms/videos/<slug>-<32-hex-id>; public folders at loom.com/share/folder/<id> are simpler. Individual recordings open at loom.com/share/<video-id>. A signed-in Loom session is required for private library folders and access-controlled recordings. Reuse an already-open tab showing the same recording rather than opening a new one.
screen_tips: Library video cards are article elements whose visible title starts with an ARIA prefix; the list virtualizes, so scroll by bringing the last visible card into view rather than by setting scroll position. The Transcript panel shows timestamped cue text next to the player. Recordings can contain several video elements, including a short preview, so pick the one with the real duration and resolution before reading frames. Seeking the player is how you confirm a frame changed; the poster image can still show while the video is at another time.

name: Lulu
planner_tips: Lulu account currency is support-managed: the owner must contact support via https://help.lulu.com/en/support/tickets/new, choosing Lulu Print API, then Account and Updating Account Information, and get the owner's authorization first. Account settings and the storefront currency selector do not change billing currency. API key credentials live at https://developers.lulu.com/api-keys and require login.
screen_tips: After the ticket form submits, look for a ticket number, acknowledgment email, or the ticket list before retrying, since a cleared form does not prove submission. The help site's suggested-answer panel may wrongly point to a settings-page change; trust the official article and the observed controls. Credential fields on the API keys page should not be copied into notes or screenshots.

name: Tongcheng (ly.com)
planner_tips: Hotel search list opens at https://www.ly.com/hotel/hotellist?city=<cityId>&inDate=YYYY-MM-DD&outDate=YYYY-MM-DD, and a hotel detail page at https://www.ly.com/hotel/hoteldetail?hotelId=<hotelId>&inDate=YYYY-MM-DD&outDate=YYYY-MM-DD. Prices only appear after logging in at https://passport.ly.com/?pageurl=<encoded target URL>, and the login persists in the browser afterward. Shanghai's city id is 321, and mobile m.ly.com scenery paths return 404, so start from the desktop site.
screen_tips: Before login, every price shows as the placeholder ￥？. After login, room cards on the hotel detail page show three prices in order: original, member price, and savings. The room list is the default tab, and you may need to scroll down or click the 房间 tab to reach it. On the hotel search page, the green 搜索 button is a plain div, so it has to be clicked directly on screen rather than through a button element. Results load slowly, so wait several seconds for the 正在搜寻更多住宿 loader to finish before reading cards.

name: Macrotrends
planner_tips: Stock price history, market cap, and fundamentals can be opened directly at macrotrends.net/stocks/charts/TICKER/company-name/ style pages, or via the stock price history page for the ticker. Economic indicator and index chart pages live at macrotrends.net/NNNN/slug URLs, and the slug is in the page URL. Most charts are public and need no login.
screen_tips: Charts load in an embedded frame and the data tables sit below them. Use the ticker symbol to find a stock quickly, and the page title to confirm you are on the right chart. Some wrapper pages may show an access error, so reloading the page or opening it again usually works.

name: Manus
planner_tips: Open https://manus.im/app to start a new task and https://manus.im/app/<taskId> to reopen a task by its id from the URL. Completed tasks can be shared at https://manus.im/share/<taskId>, which only works after the task has been shared. Manus requires a signed-in account; if the page redirects to a login or Google sign-in page, stop and ask the user to sign in.
screen_tips: The prompt box at the bottom of /app is a rich text editor, so click into it and type; the send button is the black round arrow-up at its bottom-right, and Enter can sometimes open a slash menu instead of sending. A task is finished when the page shows a line reading exactly 'Task completed' with a green check. Sidebar tasks are plain text divs rather than links, and task titles are auto-shortened, so identify tasks by their URL id. Clicking Share opens a popover with a Copy link button, and clicking Share again closes it.

name: Medium
planner_tips: For a public article, open the article URL directly, such as https://medium.com/@user/slug-abc123, and the page shows the full body when the account is logged in. Publication pages are at https://medium.com/<publication-slug> and profiles at https://medium.com/@username. Medium search pages need a logged-in session and are not reachable without one. Member-only posts show a paywall unless the browser is signed in to an account with access.
screen_tips: The article body sits inside the single article element; the clap, comment, listen and share row at the top is not body text. A paywall modal or a Sign in prompt means the article is locked for this account, so sign in or pick a different source. Text that appears short or cut off after the first paragraphs usually means the page has not finished loading, so wait a couple of seconds before reading.

name: Mermaid Live Editor
planner_tips: Open the editor with the diagram code encoded in the URL hash as #pako:<data>, where data is zlib-compressed then URL-safe base64 of the editor state JSON, not a query parameter. Plain base64 of the code opens a blank editor. No login is needed.
screen_tips: The diagram renders client-side after the page loads, so wait for a visible graph SVG and check that the editor text matches the submitted code. A blank editor with no graph means the encoding was wrong. Treat an error icon or error text in the graph area as a syntax failure.

name: Metacritic
planner_tips: Title pages open directly at metacritic.com/game/{slug}/, /movie/{slug}/ or /tv/{slug}/, where slug is the title lowercased with spaces as hyphens and punctuation dropped (for example metacritic.com/game/the-last-of-us/). Score and review pages are reached from the title page, and no login is needed to read scores or reviews. Music pages are blocked to automated access, so do not plan on music pages loading.
screen_tips: The Metascore is the large colored number on the title page, with the critic review count beside it, and the user score appears in a separate box next to it. If a title has fewer than four critic reviews, the Metascore shows as TBD instead of a number. Multi-platform games show one score by default, so use the platform selector on the page to see scores for other platforms. Search is in the top bar, and results list the media type so you can pick games, movies or TV shows.

name: Microsoft 365
planner_tips: Open https://admin.cloud.microsoft/#/Domains to manage custom domains and https://admin.cloud.microsoft/#/users to edit user addresses, and sign in with an admin account first. For DKIM settings, open https://security.microsoft.com/authentication?viewid=DKIM.
screen_tips: In the domain wizard, DNS record groups expand only through their small arrow buttons, not the heading text, so look for buttons labeled with 'records' or 'uitvouwen'. After clicking a wizard step, wait for the next heading or validation result before acting again, because transitions can finish after the page loads. In the user address dialog, changes are not saved until the final save succeeds, so reopen the user record afterward to confirm. If the domain is missing from the alias dropdown, reload the Users page.  ‑ Check the signed-in account name before any admin change, since a Chrome profile may sign into a different corporate tenant automatically.

name: MusicBrainz
planner_tips: Search artists at musicbrainz.org/search?query=NAME&type=artist, and similar type= values for release, recording, release-group, label, or work. Entity pages are musicbrainz.org/artist/MBID (replace artist with release, recording, etc.). Reads need no login.
screen_tips: Search results list entities with a score and disambiguation text under the name, so check that text to pick the right artist. Entity pages show tabs for releases, recordings, and tags, and the Cover Art Archive shows images on release pages. Search results can show the same title several times for different regional pressings, so compare date and country.

name: Namecheap
planner_tips: Open https://ap.www.namecheap.com/domains/domaincontrolpanel/<domain>/advancedns to reach a domain's Advanced DNS editor. Log in first, since the DNS pages require a Namecheap account session. Changing Mail Settings from Email Forwarding to Custom MX removes the forwarding SPF record, so plan to publish the chosen provider's SPF record separately. DNS changes can take time to appear publicly because negative answers may stay cached at some resolvers.
screen_tips: In the Advanced DNS page, use the ADD NEW RECORD link in the Host Records or Custom MX section you need. Record types are picked from a dropdown list, so choose the matching option by its text and click it. Each new row has its own save control, and the row leaves edit mode once saved; wait for that before adding another row, and blur filled fields first. Custom MX has a separate SAVE ALL CHANGES button, and if the page still shows rows but saves fail, the session may have expired, so reload and check for a login prompt.

name: NASA Open Data APIs
names: nasa astronomy picture of the day
planner_tips: These are JSON data APIs with no visual site to browse, so direct URL access is the main route; the guide says to avoid the browser entirely. Example: https://api.nasa.gov/planetary/apod?api_key=DEMO_KEY returns today's Astronomy Picture of the Day, and adding date=YYYY-MM-DD selects a specific day. Example: https://epic.gsfc.nasa.gov/api/natural lists the latest Earth images from EPIC. A personal API key from https://api.nasa.gov/ is free and raises the DEMO_KEY rate limit of about 10 requests per hour.
screen_tips: The guide's content is about JSON responses rather than page controls, so there is little to do on screen. If a page shows a rate-limit error, the DEMO_KEY hourly or daily quota is exhausted and access resumes after the reset window. EPIC and Exoplanet Archive pages have no key or rate limit.

name: News Aggregation (multi-source)
planner_tips: Open the front pages directly: https://techcrunch.com, https://www.bbc.com/news, https://www.theguardian.com/world, https://www.wired.com, https://news.ycombinator.com, https://www.nytimes.com; these pages load without a login. Reuters blocks direct page fetches, so open https://www.reuters.com in a browser and expect slow, JavaScript-heavy loading.
screen_tips: BBC may show a cookie consent banner for EU visitors; accept it or dismiss it before reading headlines. On BBC, use the article headlines (not the site labels such as 'The BBC is in multiple languages'). On TechCrunch, headlines sit in h3 elements inside the page body, and the article layout changed, so older article-card layouts may not appear. On Reuters, scroll down and wait a few seconds for the page to finish loading before reading headlines.

name: Nordic Naturals
planner_tips: Product pages live at nordic.com/products/<slug>/, and a specific size or flavor may be selected with a ?variant=<id> query parameter, so keep that parameter when opening a product. Supplement facts are only shown in a drawer on the product page, so a search result snippet or product description is not enough to confirm ingredients for a specific variant.
screen_tips: Click the visible Supplement Facts button on the product page to open a right-side drawer, and confirm the drawer titled Supplement Facts is open before reading. Read the full label in the drawer, including serving size, amounts, and other ingredients, since search snippets can omit it or mix up similarly named blends. Close the drawer with the close button labeled Close supplement facts sidebar at its top.

name: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements
planner_tips: Fact sheets open at ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/<Nutrient>-HealthProfessional/ or ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/<Nutrient>-Consumer/, choose the audience that matches the task. No login or form submission is needed for public fact sheets.
screen_tips: Confirm the audience from the visible page title and read the article body and the Updated date near the top. Inline citations pop up as tooltips, so read the displayed prose rather than the hidden citation text. Section headings are the reliable way to find a topic on a page.

name: Open Library
planner_tips: Open search results directly with https://openlibrary.org/search?q=QUERY, and use title= or author= parameters (e.g. https://openlibrary.org/search?title=dune&author=frank+herbert) for narrower matches. Work pages look like https://openlibrary.org/works/OL893415W and edition pages like https://openlibrary.org/books/OL7353617M; ISBN lookups can use https://openlibrary.org/isbn/ISBN. Browsing and reading require no login, but lists, ratings and reading logs need an Internet Archive account.
screen_tips: The search page has filter facets on the left for language, format and availability, and sort options at the top. A work page lists editions below the description, and a Read or Borrow button appears when a digital copy exists. Clicking a book title opens its work page, and the edition list shows publisher and ISBN for each printing.

name: OpenAlex
planner_tips: The site is a JSON API with no login and no browser UI needed for lookups; a person-like agent can open https://openalex.org and use its search box, or open https://openalex.org/works?search=transformer+attention to see work results directly. Entity pages follow the pattern https://openalex.org/W2626778328 (works), https://openalex.org/A5108093963 (authors), https://openalex.org/I63966007 (institutions), and https://openalex.org/S137773608 (sources). Filters can be passed as query parameters on the openalex.org list pages, for example https://openalex.org/works?filter=publication_year:2023 or https://openalex.org/works?sort=cited_by_count:desc. No account or sign-in is required.
screen_tips: The site is a free public database that needs no login; search results and filters appear on the page after typing and pressing Enter. Result counts appear above the list, and clicking a title opens the work page with its DOI, authors, and open-access links. Entity IDs shown on pages are full openalex.org URLs, and the bare ID is the last part of the URL. The browser should be used for reading pages rather than scraping; the JSON API is intended for programmatic access and is not needed for normal browsing.

name: OpenStreetMap
planner_tips: This guide covers only HTTP APIs (Nominatim geocoding and Overpass queries), not the interactive map site, so a browser is not needed for the data itself. For a place search on the map UI, open https://www.openstreetmap.org/search?query=Eiffel+Tower and for a coordinate view use https://www.openstreetmap.org/#map=15/48.8584/2.2945. No login is required.
screen_tips: On openstreetmap.org the search box is at the top left and results appear in a side panel. Clicking a result centers the map and updates the URL with the map coordinates and zoom. Action worked when the URL hash changes and the marker or highlighted feature appears on the map.'}  -- 2 to 1 error corrected below.json_placeholder_removed

name: Outlook
planner_tips: Open https://outlook.office.com/mail/ to reach the inbox; the user must be logged in to a Microsoft account. Compose a message from there, and confirm the send by checking the Sent Items folder for the exact subject and recipient, since delivery to the recipient cannot be verified from the sender side.
screen_tips: A first-use privacy dialog may appear over the inbox; dismiss its Continue button before opening compose. When typing a recipient address, select the suggestion shown below the field and confirm a recipient chip was created before moving to the Subject field, because the suggestion popup can cover it. Do not press Tab to leave a recipient field, since it can insert an invalid empty recipient; click the next field instead. A successful send closes the compose window and removes the draft.

name: npm and PyPI package registries
planner_tips: Open https://www.npmjs.com/package/NAME for a package's public page, or https://pypi.org/project/NAME/ for a Python package page. Package pages for npm and PyPI are public and need no login. Download counts for PyPI are shown on pypistats.org/packages/NAME, and npm search is at https://www.npmjs.com/search?q=TERM.
screen_tips: On npm package pages, the README is in the main column and the install command and version are in the sidebar. On PyPI project pages, the project description is central and the release history is in the sidebar, with a link to Download files lower down. pypistats.org shows download totals as charts and tables on its package page.}

name: PartSouq
planner_tips: To look up OEM parts by VIN, open https://partsouq.com/en/search/all?q=<17-char VIN>, which redirects to the manufacturer catalog for that exact vehicle. No login is needed for browsing. Dealer e-commerce sites and Toyota TIS usually lack the catalog or reject new VINs, so prefer PartSouq for this.
screen_tips: On the vehicle page, use the 'Search in vehicle' box to search by part name or 5-digit Toyota base code, such as 44250. Results show full part numbers with quantity and production-date applicability; open the figure link to see the exploded diagram. Footnote callouts marked N01 mean the part is not sold individually. Check that the production-date window covers the target vehicle before treating a part as correct.

name: Perplexity Computer
planner_tips: Open https://www.perplexity.ai/computer/tasks for the task list, and https://www.perplexity.ai/computer/connectors or /computer/skills for connectors and custom skills. A task page is at https://www.perplexity.ai/computer/tasks/<slug>-<id>, and its public view is that URL with ?view=thread appended. Sign in first, since Computer is a paid feature that spends credits.
screen_tips: Start a task by clicking the composer area (data-ask-input-container) and typing, then press Enter or the arrow send button; the URL changes to a task URL once submitted. Task rows on the list are clickable divs, not links, and the top bar has Usage, Todo and Share buttons, with Todo opening a plan panel showing check or pending icons. Share opens a popover with Private, Specific people and Anyone with the link options, and Copy Link copies the URL. An Insufficient credits banner with an Add credits button means the task is paused, not finished.

name: Polymarket
planner_tips: Event pages open at polymarket.com/event/<slug>, where the slug is the stable identifier; a market page is polymarket.com/market/<slug>, but most markets are reached through events. Viewing markets and comments needs no login, but wallet-connect prompts can appear if a previous session linked a wallet, so use a clean browser profile.
screen_tips: Each outcome row in a grouped event shows its label, a chance percentage, the Yes and No prices in cents, and volume; the first volume figure at the top is the event total, not an outcome. Price cents shown in the outcome rows are the visible values to read. Related-market cards in the sidebar show their own cents and percentages and are not part of the main event. Class names rotate and there are no data-testid attributes, so identify elements by visible text and position.

name: Product Hunt
planner_tips: Open daily launches directly at https://www.producthunt.com/leaderboard/daily/YYYY/M/D (month and day without zero padding, e.g. /2026/4/18), which lists all products for that day with vote counts. Weekly and monthly leaderboards live at /leaderboard/weekly/YYYY/WW and /leaderboard/monthly/YYYY/M. Topic pages are at /topics/<name> and search at /search?q=<terms>. No login is needed to view products. Product pages are at /products/<slug>, not /posts/.
screen_tips: Use new_tab() to open producthunt.com URLs, since direct navigation sometimes fails; wait a few seconds for the page to finish rendering. Today's vote counts show as a dash for the first 4 hours of the day, so use yesterday's leaderboard for real counts.
